newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan-China trade down 1.2 pct Jan-July yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-China trade down 1.2 pct Jan-July yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's indirect trade with China slid 1.2 percent to US$12.17 billion in the first seven months of 1996 from the same period in 1995, the Board of Foreign Trade said on Monday.
Taiwan's exports to China grew 0.2 percent to $10.45 billion, accounting for 15.8 percent of Taiwan's total exports, the board said in a statement.
Imports from China declined 8.7 percent to $1.72 billion, accounting for 2.9 percent of the island's total imports. It was the third month in a row that imports from China declined.

The board attributed the decline to China's having lowered its export rebate tax rate in January, which caused Taiwan-owned factories in China to advance their exports ahead of the change. The cut also led to a slowdown in Taiwan's processing material exports to China.
During the January-July period, Taiwan had a trade surplus of $8.73 billion with China, up 2.2 percent from the same period a year ago.

Beijing, which has considered Taiwan a renegade province since the Chinese civil war separated them in 1949, held war games in the Taiwan Strait ahead of the island's presidential elecion on March 23 to warn voters not to drop the pledge to reunify with China.
Officials have said the war games made Taiwanese less willing to invest in the mainland.
Taiwan bans direct contact with China. All trade with China must go through a third region, mostly Hong Kong. Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have invested more then US$20 billion in China.
